newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Ahmanson sees court response soon.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Ahmanson sees court response soon.

text.p: H.F. Ahmanson and Co will know within weeks if it can block a June 13 Great Western Financial Corp shareholder vote on a proposed merger with rival Washington Mutual Inc, chief executive Charles Rinehart said.
"We expect to hear somewhere toward the end of this month, or in the beginning of next month," he said in an interview.

Ahmanson Tuesday requested an injunction in Delaware Chancery Court to block the vote. It wants to delay a vote on Washington Mutual's proposal so that Great Western's board can have a chance to hear from new boardmembers elected June 13.
Ahmanson is seeking to have three directors elected to the Great Western board at the June 13 annual meeting.

On Tuesday, Great Western and Washington Mutual, which agreed to merge in order to thwart hostile bidder Ahmanson, received Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) approval of their registration statement relating to the merger proposal.

The SEC approval and scheduling of a vote on June 13 were seen as victories by Washington Mutual by some analysts who say time is of the essence for Ahmanson. Indeed, Ahmanson earlier this week decided to take its bid of up to 1.2 of its shares for each Great Western share directly to shareholders.
But before it can begin its exchange offer, Ahmanson must get clearance from the Securities and Exchange Commission.
"We expect approval in a week to ten days on our exchange offer," Rinehart said.
He said with the approval, shareholders would be able to tender their shares on Ahmanson's proposal before the shareholder vote on Washington Mutual's proposal.
Rinehart said he does not expect to change the terms of his bid, valued at about $6.9 billion based on Wednesday's share price.

"There's no reason to change our offer. We think we'll get the response (on our offer)," he said, saying that the price of its offer was somewhat higher and that there was less execution risk than under Washington Mutual's bid.
